body:
Redline round 3

Reviewed the fix diff from round 2 (54b13f1..ff5b0a8), and the coverage pass's candidates over the whole pull request at ff5b0a8.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at ff5b0a8 returned 8 candidates: 7 verified, 0 could not be confirmed, 0 refuted, 1 collapsed into items already reported or settled, 0 already tracked.

Round 2's fixes do what they set out to do: every failing step of the record write names the entry it lost, one deferred entry per finding is kept, a defer override with no entry stops at resolve, the planned tasks are read from every resolve, and the handoff names the fix-diff low findings. Most of the findings are about trusting what an agent restates. A reshape's deferral of a finding the person decided replaces or blocks the person's (R3-4, R3-6), a no-mitigation deferral listed with files takes in any commit that names it (R3-5, in round 2's fixes), and R1-7's word list misses other wordings (R3-2); the issue body also escapes code inside multi-line fields (R3-3). This repository has no scheduled commands or queued jobs, so there is no overlap to check, and the reviewer's guard refuses `node`, so the loop findings were traced through the cited lines rather than run.

### Correctness (5)

- **R3-2** · correctness · medium · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:771` · NOTHING_SHIPS reads only a fixed list of whole phrases, so another wording of 'nothing ships' still demands a commit
- **R3-3** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:1299` · A multi-line draft field is escaped whole, so a filed issue shows &lt;, &amp; and @&#8288; inside its code blocks
- **R3-4** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3124` · checkDrafts holds a reshape to a full draft for a finding the person already decided, stopping the round at shape
- **R3-5** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3730` · shaperPlanned counts a no-mitigation deferral listed with files as planned, so a commit that only names its id is posted as its mitigation
- **R3-6** · correctness · medium · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3808` · A reshape's deferred entry replaces the resolve agent's for a decided finding, undoing the person's deferral or swapping its draft

### Other items (2)

- **R3-1** · nit · low · confirmed · `agents/redline-github.md:28` · The GitHub agent's defer operation says it runs before the push, but the end-of-run filing runs after it
- **R3-7** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:4239` · humanSummary words a draft's place by hand, differently from deferredTo

Each item has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the item's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, with what it decided and why.

### Candidates set aside (1)

<details>
<summary>Refuted, collapsed or already tracked</summary>

- `workflows/redline-loop.js:2916` · When the person drops the draft of a deferral they chose themselves (a call answered 'Mitigate'), the restated reason the skill records in `args.deferrals[id].notes` is thrown away. The reply uses the call's notes and only adds 'No issue was opened.' Yet docs/running.md:129 and skills/redline/SKILL.md:224 say the drop's restatement is posted in the thread. R2-7 settled the wording; this is the narrower mismatch with the docs. The same happens at line 3422 for drafts held to the end. · settled: R2-7: declined. Its reason states this on purpose: a deferral the person chose keeps its decision sentence and, for a dropped draft, closes with 'No issue was opened.', so the drop's restatement is not posted (outcomesFor, workflows/redline-loop.js:2916, and draftClose, 2948). The skill's line saying the restatement is posted (skills/redline/SKILL.md:224) describes a Redline deferral's drop (droppedOutcome, 2939-2941).

</details>

comments.body:
**R3-1** · nit · low · confirmed

**The GitHub agent's defer operation says it runs before the push, but the end-of-run filing runs after it**

The `defer` bullet opens with "After the checker passed and before the push and the replies". With `defer at end`, `settleHeld` (workflows/redline-loop.js:3407-3415) calls `fileDeferred(pass, record, toFile, 'Finish')` once the run finishes, after each round's `push and reply` call has already pushed. `deferPrompt` (2228-2239) says nothing about when the call runs, so the agent file is the only statement of the order, and in that case it is wrong. docs/running.md, Deferred items, Filing, already states both cases ("or, with deferred items raised at the end of the run, when the run finishes"). The prompt's steps are the same either way, so nothing is filed differently; the agent is told something untrue about where it is in the run.

Proposed fix: Reword the bullet's opening as docs/running.md does: "After the checker passed and before the push and the replies, or, with deferred items raised at the end of the run, at Finish before the replies those items waited for".

**R3-2** · correctness · medium · confirmed

**NOTHING_SHIPS reads only a fixed list of whole phrases, so another wording of 'nothing ships' still demands a commit**

R1-7 was fixed, but still reproduces here with a wording outside the list. `NOTHING_SHIPS` is `^(none|n\/a|nothing|nothing ships( now)?|no mitigation)(\s*\(.*\))?\.?$`: only those words, optionally a parenthesised note and a full stop, to the end of the string. `None; nothing ships in this pull request.` and `N/A — the full fix is deferred` fail at the `;` and the dash, so `hasMitigation` (772-775) returns true. For a shaper deferral, `mitigated` (3874) is then true and `needCommits` (3875-3876) demands a commit naming the finding, which the plan has no task for, since the shaper planned nothing to ship. `judge` (2459) reports `no commit names R1-2`, the repair pass has nothing to build, and the run stops at stage `check`; a resume replays the cached shape and stops the same way. The same reading makes `describeOutcome` post the phrase as `mitigation: ...` (2960) and `draftView` show it as what ships (3361). It needs the shaper or the resolve agent to write the field in words, which the shape prompt invites by asking the recommendation beside it to say "that nothing ships now" (1932); the prompts ask for an empty string (1989, 2029). Traced; the reviewer's guard refuses `node`, so the loop test was not run.

Proposed fix: Stop deciding 'ships something' from free text alone: a deferral demands a commit only when it ships a mitigation and a task with files was planned for it (`plannedTask(id) || shaperPlanned(id)`), so a wording the list misses costs a mis-worded reply at most, never a stopped round; or widen the test to a leading word followed by any punctuation (`^(none|n\/a|nothing|no mitigation)\b`). A loop check: a shaper deferral with mitigation 'None; nothing ships in this pull request.' and no commit ends in status done, with no 'no commit names' error.

**R3-3** · correctness · low · confirmed

**A multi-line draft field is escaped whole, so a filed issue shows &lt;, &amp; and @&#8288; inside its code blocks**

`issueDraft` passes `found`, `why` and `fullFix` each through `postedText` (1299, 1302, 1303). `textParts` (1218-1221) treats any text holding a newline as one part, escaped whole, code spans included. A `found` written for a reader who has not seen the pull request, with a fenced block such as ```` ```php\nif ($a < $b && $c) { /** @param int */ }\n``` ````, becomes `if ($a < $b && $c) { /** @⁠param int */ }` inside the fence. GitHub shows character references literally inside a code block or span, so the filed issue's code reads `<`, `&&` and `@⁠param`, and a single-line span in any multi-line field does the same. The function's comment (1288-1289) says "a code span stays as written", which holds only for one-line fields. The escape-whole rule for a newline is #87's, accepted there as a cost for review text, and decision 13 of this pull request's spec routed the issue body through the same function; issue bodies are where multi-line text with code is common. With `defer to print`, the same escaped body is what the session prints for pasting into another tracker (`deferredEntry`, 3348). #88 tracks a newline in comment descriptions, proposed fixes and replies, not the issue body.

Proposed fix: Escape the issue body by Markdown block: leave fenced code blocks (and the spans of each line) as written and run `postedText` over the remaining lines one at a time, so a newline is no longer a reason to escape a span; or escape only outside fences and spans whatever the newlines. A loop check: a draft whose found holds a fenced block with `<`, `&` and `@param` files that block unchanged while the prose around it is escaped.

**R3-4** · correctness · low · confirmed

**checkDrafts holds a reshape to a full draft for a finding the person already decided, stopping the round at shape**

After a bounced plan, the reshape is vetted by `vetShape` (3798, 3536-3553), whose `checkDrafts` (3123-3129) throws for every finding the result marks `defer` whose entry lacks a draft field. Nothing exempts a finding in `roundDecisions`. When the person answered call R1-2 'Mitigate', the resolve agent wrote it under `## Deferred` in shape.md and returned its full draft. If the reshape, reading that shape.md, lists R1-2 as `defer` with `found` empty, the run ends with status error, stage shape: "the shaper deferred R1-2 with no drafted issue (missing found)", resumable at the reshape, even though the person's deferral and its draft were complete. The rule this pull request's standards state is that a decided finding is theirs "whatever disposition a reshape later gives it" (agent-os/standards/workflow/agents.md, line 40; the comment at 3649-3651). The reshape prompt (1987) tells the shaper a decision the person made stays as it is, so this needs the reshape to restate a decided finding as a deferral and leave its draft short. Traced through 3795-3798 and 3123-3127; not run, since the reviewer's guard refuses `node`.

Proposed fix: Skip decided findings in `checkDrafts` on a reshape (pass `roundDecisions`, or filter `shaped.findings` by `!roundDecisions[f.id]`), and drop the reshape's entry for such a finding with a warning, as `checkDispositions` drops a stray one.

**R3-5** · correctness · low · confirmed

**shaperPlanned counts a no-mitigation deferral listed with files as planned, so a commit that only names its id is posted as its mitigation**

Round 2's fix for R2-6 added `shaperPlanned` (3730), true for any shaper deferral with a non-empty `files`, whatever its mitigation, and passes it into `outcomesFor`'s `planned` (3952). There `shipsNothing` (2906) is false for such a finding, so `shipped` is every commit that names the id (`named`, 2899), including one that only mentions it. A deferral with mitigation '' and `files: ['app/y.php']` but no task, and a standards commit `redline: record the round 1 review lessons in the standards, finishing R1-2 (#3)` (the form agents/redline-implementer.md:19 gives), reply `deferred to #301. Mitigated in <sha> (redline: record the round 1 review lessons in the standards, finishing R1-2 (#3)).` R1-2 then counts in `fixed` (4024, commits non-empty), so `fixedAny` (4849) can send the run into a final nit pass over a standards-only change. Before round 2 the zeroing at 2906 ruled this out, which is what R1-10's fix meant it to do (its comment at 2902-2905). Round 2's shape.md (Unattended answer 10 and decision 3) weighed only the gate ("a shaper that lists files by mistake stops nothing"), not the reply and the count. It needs the shaper to list files for a deferral it plans no task for, against its rule that `files` are the task's paths, and some commit to name the id. Traced; not run, since the reviewer's guard refuses `node`.

Proposed fix: Count a shaper deferral as planned only when a commit's `finding` field is the id, or only when it ships a mitigation or the plan's task list names it; or keep `shaperPlanned` and leave commits that only mention the id (`mentions`) out of `shipped` when the mitigation is empty. A loop check: a shaper deferral with mitigation '' and files, whose only commit naming it is the standards commit, replies `deferred to #301.` with no Mitigated clause and buys no final nit pass.

**R3-6** · correctness · medium · confirmed

**A reshape's deferred entry replaces the resolve agent's for a decided finding, undoing the person's deferral or swapping its draft**

After a bounced plan, line 3808 rebuilds `deferred` as `shaped.deferred.concat(...)`, so the reshape's entry for an id replaces the earlier one with no exception for a finding in `roundDecisions`. `isDeferral` (3738-3747) reads that entry for a decided finding: `resolveDeferred.has(d.id) && (hasMitigation(d) || !plannedTask(d.id))`. Say the person answers call R1-2 'Mitigate' and the resolve agent returns its entry (mitigation 'a guard', its draft) with a task with files. If the reshape lists R1-2 as `defer` with mitigation '', its entry wins: `hasMitigation` is false and `plannedTask` is true, so `isDeferral` is false. No `file deferred r1` call is made, no issue is opened, and `outcomesFor` (2916) finds no `deferredItem`, so the reply is `The author ships a guard now. Applied in <sha>.` with no `Deferred to #N`. If the reshape's entry has a mitigation but another draft, the reshape's title and body replace the resolve's: `draftsOf` recomposes it (3586-3593), and it is raised again as a new version or, on autopilot, filed as the reshape wrote it. The comment at 3649-3651 says a reshape's entry never shows a decided call's deferral (#94, R8-6), and the person's decision should stand whatever a reshape lists. Line 3808 predates this pull request (#94); the readings of the entry's mitigation and draft that make it matter are this pull request's (R1-10's `resolveDeferred` test, and the drafts). It needs a bounce and a reshape that restates a decided finding's deferral differently, which the reshape prompt (1987) tells it not to do. Traced; not run, since the reviewer's guard refuses `node`.

Proposed fix: At 3808 keep the earlier entry for an id in `roundDecisions` (or in `resolveDeferred`) and drop the reshape's for it with a warning, e.g. `shaped.deferred.filter((d) => !roundDecisions[d.id])` before the concat. A loop check: a call answered 'Mitigate' with a resolve entry, then a bounce whose reshape defers the finding with mitigation '', still files the resolve's draft and replies `... Deferred to #301.`

**R3-7** · nit · low · confirmed

**humanSummary words a draft's place by hand, differently from deferredTo**

`humanSummary` writes ``${id} deferred to the draft at `path` `` (4239), while `deferredTo` (1318), which the replies and the handoff use, writes ``deferred; the issue draft is at `path` ``. A human review pass with `defer to spec` posts the summary in one wording and the thread reply in the other, and a later change to the wording has to be made in both places. The issue form (`deferred to #N`) is the same in both.

Proposed fix: Build the summary's part from the helper: `${id} ${deferredTo(record.filed[id])}`.
